overview: Sigma 4.11's LongJump is a movement booster with five selectable modes (NCP, Hypixel, Mineplex, Cubecraft, Custom), where Mineplex and Cubecraft are premium-addon-gated and notify the user before toggling off when the addon is absent. The bypassable modes all run the same stage machine off EventJump and the pre-phase of EventUpdate: the first on-ground tick with movement input calls the vanilla jump() and sets stage 1, then every airborne tick computes a horizontal speed from a per-mode base plus the speed-potion effect, decays it with an air-time counter (air / 25), and overwrites motionX/motionZ through MoveUtils.setMotion while forcing motionY from hard-coded trajectory arrays. The NCP and Hypixel modes set jumpMovementFactor to 0 to remove vanilla air control, and the GLIDE toggle stamps onGround true during stages 1-3 so the fall distance never accumulates; the NCP mode additionally zeroes lastReportedPosY every tick to blind a server-side moved-too-quickly comparison. The Custom mode inverts the design: it zeroes the horizontal motion in air and raises jumpMovementFactor to the BOOST setting, riding vanilla's jump-movement mechanic instead of overriding motion. A static vclip1() helper lifts the player exactly one block through three C04 position packets. onDisable restores motion and jumpMovementFactor per mode and resets mc.timer.timerSpeed, and the OFF setting auto-disables the module on the first landing.

sections.p: onEvent registers EventUpdate and EventJump. The EventJump pre-phase raises the jump's motionY to 0.425 (identical with or without glide), a near-vanilla value. EventUpdate pre dispatches on the MODE Options string, and every branch re-reads the setting each tick to also drive the module suffix. State is three counters - air, groundTicks and stage - reset in onEnable. The landing auto-disable lives inside the ground trigger: when OFF is set and groundTicks is already positive, the module toggles itself off instead of starting a second jump. onDisable restores what the module changed: Mineplex halves the horizontal motion and restores jumpMovementFactor 0.3, Cubecraft zeroes it, and the default branch (NCP, Hypixel, Custom) zeroes motion and jumpMovementFactor before timerSpeed is forced back to 1f.

Both modes set stage 1 and call jump() on the ground trigger. In air, the speed starts from a base (NCP: 0.75 + speedEffect * 0.2; glide: 0.8 + speedEffect * 0.2; Hypixel: 0.95 + speedEffect * 0.2; glide: 1.1 + speedEffect * 0.2), subtracts air / 25, and is clamped to MoveUtils.defaultSpeed() (0.2873 scaled by the speed-potion amplifier), with glide additionally pinning the speed to defaultSpeed() while stage < 4. MoveUtils.setMotion(speed) then projects the pressed keys onto motionX/motionZ at that magnitude. Vertical motion comes from getMotion (glide, a 30-entry array starting 0.396, -0.122, -0.1, 0.423, ...) or getOldMotion (two 12-entry arrays, one for moving and one for stationary/collided, starting 0.345, 0.2699, ...), indexed by stage--. jumpMovementFactor is forced to 0 every air tick so the vanilla sprint-jump air control cannot add or remove speed. The glide branch also writes mc.thePlayer.onGround = true while stage is between 1 and 3, so the client-side fall distance resets and the sent C03 packets claim ground in the opening arc.

Custom takes the opposite path: on the ground trigger it keeps the existing motion, and in air it zeroes motionX/motionZ, sets jumpMovementFactor to the BOOST setting (default 1, range 0.1-5, floored at 0.28), and accumulates air at x2 * BOOST * 2 per tick so the decay outruns the boost over long flights. The result is a burst of vanilla air-control speed that decays over roughly a second. vclip1 is a standalone static helper that queues three C04 position packets at +0.42, +0.753 and +1.0 blocks, then calls setPosition and sets onGround true - a one-block vertical lift used by other Sigma modules. Its C04 burst matters to the countering checks below because it is three position packets in a single tick with no physics behind them.

files.label: LongJump.java (module)
files.explanation:
The whole bypass lives in this one file. EventUpdate pre contains the per-mode branches: the ground trigger (move input, onGround, auto-disable check, jump(), stage = 1), the air-speed computation with the air/25 decay and defaultSpeed clamp, the setMotion horizontal write, the getMotion/getOldMotion vertical write, and the jumpMovementFactor zeroing. The NCP branch adds lastReportedPosY = 0 and the glide onGround spoof; the Custom branch uses jumpMovementFactor = max(BOOST, 0.28) and the doubled air accumulator; vclip1 queues the three C04s. EventJump raises motionY to 0.425, and onDisable restores motion, jumpMovementFactor and timerSpeed by mode.

The two motion tables are the fingerprint of the module server-side: getMotion's 30-entry glide table (0.396, -0.122, -0.1, 0.423, 0.35, ...) and getOldMotion's 12-entry tables (0.345, 0.2699, 0.183, ...) produce a vertical profile no vanilla jump follows, and the air/25 decay with the defaultSpeed clamp produces a horizontal profile no ground-friction model produces.

files.label: MoveUtils.java (motion helpers)
files.explanation:
MoveUtils is the shared motion toolkit the module leans on. setMotion(double speed) reads movementInput.moveForward and moveStrafe, adjusts the yaw by 45 degrees for diagonals, and projects motionX/motionZ from the resulting yaw - so every air tick the player is accelerated to an absolute speed regardless of the previous motion, which is what makes the longjump hold its speed without strafe-jumping. defaultSpeed() returns 0.2873 scaled by the move-speed potion amplifier (1.0 + 0.2 * (amplifier + 1)), the floor the module clamps its decaying speed to. getSpeedEffect() returns the same amplifier value, and isOnGround(double height) ray-casts the block under the player - the ground test the module uses instead of the raw flag.

These helpers matter because they are shared across Sigma's movement modules (the same setMotion/defaultSpeed pair drives the Speed and Fly modules), which is why the countering checks below see the longjump as a generic above-baseline speed violation rather than anything module-specific.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's physics envelope from the world instead of trusting the packet. The horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation and the vertical allowance from vDistRel, and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0)) * 100 with a set-back to the stored location. vDistRel initializes the allowed vertical distance from the previous move's momentum and only accepts a few named envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up and a riptide launch - and critically, fromOnGround/toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), a ray trace of the actual block cache, never from the packet flag.

Every LongJump mode violates one of the two axes. The NCP and Hypixel speed formulas floor at 0.75-1.1 + speed effect and only decay by air/25, so after a few ticks the horizontal distance per move exceeds the sprint-based envelope and hDistanceAboveLimit grows; the vertical tables (0.345, 0.2699, ... then negative values that never match gravity's -0.08 per-tick decay) put yDistanceAboveLimit into the violation sum at the same time. The glide spoof does not help: NCP ray-traces ground, so the claimed onGround true over open air does not relax the envelope, and the one exception - the landing auto-disable - is exactly the moment the envelope would accept the move. Only the first two or three ticks of a jump are inside the envelope, which is why the check survives on servers with it disabled and nothing else.

countering.label: Speed (base move speed envelope)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed check compares the horizontal distance of each move against a base move speed of 0.2873 scaled by speed-potion amplifiers, with per-surface modifiers for ice, slime blocks, slabs and stairs. The airborne path computes expected = baseMove + stage (0.049, 0.08 or 0.3261 depending on the jump phase) plus any pending velocity contribution, and flags when thisMove exceeds it; any move over 8 blocks is cancelled outright. Ground moves are checked against thisMove / groundTicks + baseMove once the player has been grounded for at least 5 ticks.

The NCP and Hypixel modes sit well above the airborne ceiling: their speed holds at 0.75-1.1 plus effect for the first air ticks before the air/25 decay pulls it down, versus an expected of roughly 0.2873 + 0.08 in the climbing phase, so thisMove > expected fires as soon as the stage machine is past the initial jump arc. The Custom mode's jumpMovementFactor boost produces the same excess through vanilla air control. The stage-3+ decay eventually brings the speed under the ceiling, which is why short hops and the first jump tick pass - the check needs the sustained above-base horizontal motion the module is built to produce.

countering.label: Speed (previous-speed progression model)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Speed check is a progression model: 'if your previous speed was X then your current speed must not exceed f(X)'. It computes speed from the 2D move delta, derives expected = friction * lastSpeed * handleMultipliers + (maxForce + handleAdders + epsilon) where the multipliers fold in hit slowdown, soul sand, webs and slime, and accumulates the positive discrepancy until it exceeds DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD, then punishes with a rubber-band. Accepted knockback moves and flying are skipped.

The module's air ticks violate the progression because setMotion overwrites motionX/motionZ to an absolute magnitude every tick instead of letting friction decay the previous speed: lastSpeed is high, but the expected value assumes friction multiplied it down, while the module's next move is again at 0.75-1.1. The discrepancy is positive every air tick, so the accumulator crosses the threshold within a few ticks of the jump. The same model is what the module's own air/25 decay approximates - it decays slower than ground friction, and the check's expectation is built around the vanilla decay curve, so the mismatch is structural rather than marginal.

countering.label: GroundSpoof (claimed ground vs predicted ground)
countering.explanation:
Grim's GroundSpoof compares the onGround flag the client claims in its flying packets against the ground state Grim's own prediction produced: claimed = player.clientClaimsLastOnGround, and if claimed != player.onGround it flags with a set-back and flips the NoFall check's ground status so the fall damage logic is forced server-side. Exemptions cover spectator mode, a long list of exemptOnGround states, ghost-block setbacks and the tick after a teleport.

The GLIDE toggle is a direct target: while stage is between 1 and 3 the module writes onGround true into the player state every tick, so the C03 stream claims ground over open air, and Grim's prediction - which knows the player is falling - sees claimed true against predicted false and flags. The NCP and Hypixel modes without glide never spoof ground, so they do not trip this check; their horizontal excess is handled by the prediction engine's offset accumulation instead. The one-tick exemption after a teleport does not help, because the module spoofs ground for three consecutive stages, not one tick.
